quote: A lot of what looks like a deep psychedelic crisis is a scared person in a room that's getting on their nerves
gap: How does a room getting on someone's nerves end up looking like a deep crisis: does the drug make small annoyances feel much bigger than they would sober?
note: explained earlier in the guide, in the body section before Psychological First Aid: "The body feels awful and the altered mind writes cosmic horror to explain it. Nausea, heat, exhaustion, dehydration, overstimulation, and sleep loss all become spiritual content very quickly."

quote: Switch the overhead light off and leave a lamp on.
gap: What is this for: is bright light what bothers them, and if so, why leave a lamp on instead of making the room dark?
note: the sentence before says why: a room getting on their nerves, and the light is the first thing in it; the lamp keeps a scared person out of the dark, which an earlier read of these words asked about

quote: check whether they're too hot or too cold, or desperate for the bathroom
gap: Why do I have to check: wouldn't they tell me, or can someone who is tripping not notice these things, or not say them?
note: explained earlier in the guide, in the body section before Psychological First Aid: "The body feels awful and the altered mind writes cosmic horror to explain it. Nausea, heat, exhaustion, dehydration, overstimulation, and sleep loss all become spiritual content very quickly." They may not notice what's wrong, which is why the reader checks.

quote: Songs can turn scary halfway through, so change any that do
gap: How does a song turn scary: is it something in the song itself, or the way the drug makes them hear it? And if it sounds fine to me, how do I tell it has turned scary for them?
note: what the reader does is the same either way: change the song when it scares them (they'll see it on the person); how the altered mind turns things frightening is in the guide's body section, before this one
